title: EARLIER in a calculated column: rank by counting the rows with a larger value, plus 1
query: DEFINE COLUMN Product[Price Rank] = COUNTROWS ( FILTER ( Product, EARLIER ( Product[Price] ) < Product[Price] ) ) + 1
EVALUATE SELECTCOLUMNS ( Product, "Product", Product[Product], "Rank", Product[Price Rank] ) ORDER BY [Product]

source.quote: The COUNTROWS function counts the rows of the filtered table and assigns that value to the new calculated column in the current row plus 1.
source.supports: the page gives this formula for a rank column and explains EARLIER as the value of the current row of the outer loop

source.quote: Adding 1 is needed to prevent the top ranked value from become a Blank.
source.supports: the top row has no larger value: BLANK + 1 = 1

derivation: Prices: Bike 100, Helmet 20, Lock 10, Scooter 50. Rows with a larger price: Bike none (COUNTROWS of an empty table is BLANK, BLANK + 1 = 1), Scooter 1 (Bike) + 1 = 2, Helmet 2 (Bike, Scooter) + 1 = 3, Lock 3 + 1 = 4.
